chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a person in ihram whose leg broke: what is permissible for him and what is incumbent upon him? He said, 'He is permissible from everything.' I said, 'From women, clothing, and perfume?' He said, 'Yes, from all that which is forbidden to the person in ihram.'
And he said, 'Has it not reached you the saying of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
And free me where You have detained me, for the decree You have decreed upon me.
I said, 'May God perfect you, what do you say about Hajj?' He said, 'He must perform Hajj next year.'

He said. I said, 'Then inform me about the Mahsur (one prevented from completing Hajj) and the Masdud (one prevented from entering Mecca); are they the same?' He said, 'No.' I said, 'Then inform me about the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) when the polytheists turned him back; he completed his Umrah.' He said, 'No, but he performed Umrah after that.'

key_terms.مَحْصُورٌ: One who is prevented from completing the Hajj rites
key_terms.مَصْدُودٌ: One who is prevented from entering Mecca
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: Person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What are the exemptions and obligations for a pilgrim in ihram who breaks their leg?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes that a pilgrim whose *ihram* is broken by a valid excuse, such as a leg fracture, is released from most prohibitions (*halal min kulli shay*), including wearing sewn garments and using perfume, while retaining the obligation to complete the pilgrimage. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between the *Mahsur* (prevented from completing rites) and the *Masdud* (prevented from entering Mecca), noting they are not legally equivalent, and references the Prophet’s (PBUH) precedent of performing Umrah after being turned back by the Quraysh to illustrate the flexibility in ritual completion.
